content.text:
The visual  fidelity and look and feel of the character creation screen needs to be applied broadly to the rest of the games UX. My gut says that migrating the CSS alone would be a massive improvement.

Objective:

Make the games UX consistent with the character creation screen.

NOTE: character creation had early special attention and so is ahead visually of the rest of the game.
SCOPE: if there are other UX or quality of llife improvements you want to make whille doing this that is okay.

I’ll use the repo’s Entire guidance first so the UI changes are grounded in the project’s prior intent, then I’ll inspect the character creation styling and the current runtime UI surfaces before editing.
Entire is available as the intended context source for exploration. I’m checking the repository state and UI entry points next so I can keep the diff scoped and avoid stepping on unrelated work.

The worktree appears clean from the short status output. I found the UI code is mostly JavaScript plus `index.html`, so I’m looking for the character creation CSS tokens/classes and the older overlay/HUD styles that can inherit them.

content.text: The character creation screen is using a warmer smoke/steel palette with translucent panels, soft inset highlights, and restrained borders; the rest of the UI is still mostly hard blue panels. I’m going to centralize those character-creation tokens in the shared overlay helpers first, then touch the HUD/action controls that still hard-code the old look.
